clue.text: Seeing the lady minus about one, he took a hand at bridge

definitions.text: he took a hand at bridge

parts.note: the lady is referred to as 'her'

indicators.note: the word minus goes round the letter for one, enclosing it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone notices a woman missing a player, so a man sits in for a hand of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is not the card game: in Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome, Herminius was one of the three who held the bridge with Horatius. 'about' puts I inside MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macaulay's poem Herminius helped Horatius defend the Tiber crossing against the Etruscans.

clue.text: Musical instruments provided for dances

definitions.meaning: old wind instruments with a horn bell
lively solo dances associated with sailors

explanation.surface: Instruments supplied for the dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a folk wind instrument and the brisk sailors' dance once played on it.

clue.text: Proportion returned is one in eight — that's about it

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
the word for one in eight goes round the word it

parts.note: a rowing eight has eight oars, so one of its crew is an oar
taken as written

explanation.surface: One in eight is roughly the proportion, someone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in eight' looks like the ratio itself, but it is OAR, a single rower of an eight. 'about' puts IT inside OAR to give OITAR, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two amounts, a proportion.

clue.text: Perhaps visionary ladies are involved in it

indicators.note: the jumbled ladies sit inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters of ladies are mixed

explanation.surface: Dreamy women are mixed up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are involved' rearranges LADIES to DEALIS, which 'in' places inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is one example of someone guided by high ideals.

clue.text: Mean to include the governor finally

indicators.note: the word for mean takes in the letters for the governor

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
HE is His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: A plan to bring in the governor at last.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for eventually, after everything has been taken into account.

clue.text: There's half a mast in such a tree

indicators.note: the half of mast is placed within the word such
half of mast is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Half a ship's mast is made from a particular tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes MA from MAST, and 'in' places it inside SUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shrub or tree of the cashew family, also spelt with no final H.

clue.text: Hat seen in ghetto ? Questionable

indicators.note: the letters are visible inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A doubtful headpiece spotted in a poor quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless cap, like a chef's.

clue.text: Struggle for reform results right away

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
right is R, and away tells you to drop that letter from results

explanation.surface: Campaigning to change the outcome at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from RESULTS, leaving ESULTS, which 'reform' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or fight.

clue.text: Appears as if mood changes this Sunday

parts.note: quasi is Latin for as if, meaning seemingly

indicators.note: changes means the letters of mood are put in another order

explanation.surface: It seems as though the mood shifts on this particular Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns MOOD into MODO. Low Sunday, the first after Easter, takes its name from the Latin introit 'Quasi modo geniti'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Sunday after Easter is named from the opening words of its Latin introit.

clue.text: Part of Lear written by Poe?

definitions.meaning: Gloucester's legitimate son, a role in Shakespeare's King Lear
the first name of the American author, so it was by him

explanation.surface: A section of Lear penned by Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: A role in Shakespeare's tragedy and the first name of Allan Poe, who wrote his works.

clue.text: Might be beaten by any weakling

definitions.text: Might be beaten by any weakling

parts.words: Might be beaten by any weakling
parts.note: read as a weakling's defeat, but the thing beaten is what a coward beats when withdrawing in haste

explanation.surface: Something so feeble that even a weakling could overcome it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is 'to beat a retreat', to withdraw, which a weakling will readily do.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies and cowards 'beat' a withdrawal, the idiom being drummed backward movement.

clue.text: Has to change one nag for another

parts.note: has to means must

indicators.note: the word nag is altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider forced to swap one tired horse for a fresh one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one nag for another' reads as a horse swap; the definition is 'another', a second nag, i.e. a different horse. 'change' rearranges NAG to ANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains, so it is another kind of nag.

clue.text: Where Gray's Youth was a learner, in search for plunder

parts.note: Thomas Gray's poem The Bard has 'Youth at the prow, and Pleasure at the helm'
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A youngster in an old poem, still an apprentice, out looking for loot.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Gray's The Bard; British learner drivers display a red L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to roam stealthily hunting for prey or booty.

clue.text: A U device in the Alps?

definitions.text: A U device in the Alps?

parts.words: A U device in the Alps?
parts.note: U is the upper-class tag, so an 'upper' or 'higher' motto, recalling the strange device on the banner carried through an Alpine village in Longfellow's poem

explanation.surface: A U-shaped gadget somewhere in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: In Longfellow's poem a youth carries a banner 'with the strange device' through the Alps; the Latin word on it means 'higher', and U stands for upper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means ever upward, the banner's legend in Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: Commendation is quietly uplifting

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
uplifting means lifting up, raising

explanation.surface: Praise that is soft-spoken yet heartening.
explanation.definitionFit: Commendation is the act of speaking well of someone, as is lauding.

clue.text: Character in Stalky & Co.

parts.note: Kipling's school story, but the character meant is the printed symbol in its title

explanation.surface: A boy from Kipling's school stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Stalky & Co. is Kipling's book of schoolboys; the character is not a person but the '&' symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol & is a typographic sign meaning 'and'.

clue.text: Noted price of Omar's reputation

parts.note: in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam the poet 'sold my reputation for' a cheap price, which is also something set to musical notes

explanation.surface: The well-known cost of a Persian poet's good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat line is 'And sold my Reputation for a Song'; 'Noted' means written in musical notes, not famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell for a trifle is to sell 'for a song', a piece of music with notes.

clue.text: They may look as if they do, but they don't

definitions.text: They may look as if they do, but they don't

parts.words: They may look as if they do, but they don't
parts.note: artificial eyeballs appear to look, yet cannot see

explanation.surface: A riddle about things that seem one way and are another.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial eyes made of glass resemble real ones but give no sight.

clue.text: This staff for museum's prehistoric animals section ?

definitions.text: This staff for museum's prehistoric animals section ?

parts.words: This staff for museum's prehistoric animals section ?
parts.note: the minimum crew needed to run a place, which also describes the bony frames shown in a dinosaur hall

explanation.surface: Staffing levels for a museum's dinosaur gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare-minimum crew is a skeleton staff, and a fossil gallery is full of skeletons.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimal crew is called a skeleton staff, and bony frames fill a fossil hall.

clue.text: Uplifting strains

parts.note: music that raises an audience to its feet, since people stand when it is played

explanation.surface: Inspiring music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' means making people stand up, as audiences do for this tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's official patriotic song, for which crowds rise.

clue.text: Number of foreigners in part of tribe

definitions.meaning: a clan, a division of a tribe, especially in Ireland

explanation.surface: A headcount of outsiders within a tribal group.
explanation.definitionFit: French for seven, and a word for a clan or family branch within a larger people.

clue.text: Musical state

definitions.meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show
a US state in the south central plains

explanation.surface: A tuneful frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show and the American state it is named after.

clue.text: See 18
Cooking is rare in this range

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling with, so is and rare are rearranged

explanation.surface: Underdone meat on this kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged chain of mountains.

clue.text: Never failing to get picked ?

parts.note: always selected, but read as a garden flower that returns every year to be cut again

explanation.surface: A player who is always chosen for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team selection; the word means everlasting and also names a plant that flowers year after year, so is picked again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Means lasting or recurring constantly, and names plants living through many seasons.

clue.text: Something Horner grasped about one Roman weapon

indicators.note: the fruit goes round the letter for one

parts.note: Little Jack Horner, in the nursery rhyme, put in his thumb and pulled out a plum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Roman spear that a nursery-rhyme boy got hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Jack Horner is a nursery rhyme. 'about' wraps PLUM round I.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilum was the heavy javelin of the Roman legionary.

clue.text: Clubs decreasingly used?

parts.note: golf clubs with metal heads, numbered so that loft grows as the number falls, and also something used to press clothes less and less

explanation.surface: Golf clubs falling out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid as printed has IRANS, an OCR misread of O as A; the crossing 25-down is OMENS, which confirms O.
explanation.definitionFit: These are metal-headed golf clubs, numbered by loft.

clue.text: Signs that in Rome no one backs Bob

indicators.note: backs means the Latin word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: nemo is Latin, the language of Rome, for no one
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A Roman nobody supports Bob, which is telling.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid's AMENS is an OCR misread: NEMO turned round is OMEN. A bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are signs of what is to come.

clue.text: Material gets used at last:…

parts.note: a hide only becomes usable stuff at the end of processing, which the next clue continues

explanation.surface: Cloth is finally put to use, as the story continues.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 27-across: the material is hide that is finally usable once tanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal hide is a material for shoes, belts and bags.

clue.text: … prepared here from yarn, ten varieties

indicators.note: varieties means different arrangements of the letters of yarn and ten

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the material is made from yarn in ten kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 26-across: the previous clue's material (hide) is prepared here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is the works where hides are cured into finished stock.

clue.text: She returns by herself

indicators.note: reading backwards on her own she gives the same letters, so the word is its own reversal

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman who comes back alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite form of address for a woman, so a female person.

clue.text: Girl is inclined to employ chroniclers

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a ship that lists leans to one side, is inclined

explanation.surface: A young woman tends to take on record-keepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of yearly records of events, historians of each year.
